newsitem.title: PERU: Lima stocks end slightly down in rudderless trade.
newsitem.headline: Lima stocks end slightly down in rudderless trade.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed down slightly in low volume Friday in rudderless trade as most investors remained sidelined due to worries over the economy's slow growth, brokers said.
They added the market was likely to continue its recent trend, seeing slipping prices and small volumes next week.
Friday, the General Index fell 0.03 percent to 1,441.8 points, and the blue-chip Selective Index dropped 0.50 percent to 2,012.0 points, according to preliminary stock figures.

The market has drifted for weeks because investors, disappointed at recent economic growth figures, have not been encouraged to buy Peruvian equities. But they are also prepared to wait on the sidelines because they expect the economy to pick up early next year, brokers said.
"There is nothing to justify any sustained demand for stocks nor anything to cause a big sell," said Luis Calderon of the local brokerage Acciones y Valores.
Earlier this week, Economy Minister Jorge Camet told Congress the government estimated the economy would grow around 2.5 percent this year, down from 7.0 percent last year.
But he added the first quarter next year would see a sharp acceleration of the growth rate leading to an overall gross domestic product rise of five percent in 1997.
Friday, benchmark Telefnica del Per closed down 0.96 percent at 5.16 soles, in volume of 2.039 million shares, according to preliminary figures.
Tin miner Minsur corrected some of its losses suffered Thursday, climbing 1.61 percent to 22.10 soles on volume of 30,000 shares.
Electricity distributor Luz del Sur, which saw the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start Monday, climbed 3.82 percent to 3.53 soles on volume of 210,000 shares.
In a total of 1,206 trades, volume was estimated at 32.5 million soles ($12.6 million)
